title: How Do Students Bloom? Re-considering Maslow’s Hierarchy of Needs in Educational Settings
titleZh: 学生如何绽放？重新审视教育情境中的马斯洛需求层次理论
abstract: Abstract The educational maxim “Children must Maslow before they Bloom” has become a widely accepted folk pedagogy for understanding student motivation and learning. Drawing on Abraham Maslow's hierarchy of needs and Benjamin Bloom's taxonomy of educational objectives, the phrase is commonly used to justify the assumption that students must satisfy basic needs before meaningful intellectual engagement can occur. We argue that this interpretation represents a particular reading of Maslow rather than a complete account of his theory. Examining educational textbooks, teacher preparation materials, and professional discourse, we show how hierarchical distinctions between “higher” and “lower” needs are frequently translated into assumptions about readiness, capacity, and academic potential. We further suggest that these interpretations are reinforced by broader hierarchical and individualistic assumptions embedded within the conceptual vocabulary available to Maslow. Drawing on Indigenous perspectives, the Medicine Wheel, and Relational Developmental Systems metatheory, we propose a non-hierarchical, relational framework that preserves Maslow’s humanistic aspirations while offering a more equitable understanding of motivation, learning, and human flourishing.
summaryZh: 作者指出“儿童必须先马斯洛再布鲁姆”这一说法已成为广泛接受的民间教育学，被用来为基本需求先于智力投入的假设辩护。 作者认为教育材料常把“高/低”需求的层级区分转译为关于准备度、能力与学业潜力的假设。 作者提出这些解读被马斯洛可用概念词汇中更广泛的层级化与个体主义预设所强化。 作者提出一种非层级、关系性的框架，以保留马斯洛的人本主义目标并给出更公平的动机、学习与人类繁荣理解。
